articles.title: The minimum wage is pricing young workers out of jobs
articles.summary: The triple lock was the most revered sacred cow in British politics. Economists warned that it was unsustainable, but ministers looked away, too afraid of th...
articles.body:
The triple lock was the most revered sacred cow in British politics. Economists warned that it was unsustainable, but ministers looked away, too afraid of the electoral consequences of being honest about the burgeoning cost of the state pension.

But now that Andy Burnham has suggested that he would reform the mechanism – albeit after the next election – the title of "most untouchable policy" seems to have changed hands.

The negative effects of dramatically increasing the minimum wage , and in particular the youth rate paid to 18 to 20-year-olds, are now undeniable. Youth unemployment is at a 10-year high, in no small part because employers have been put off from hiring inexperienced but increasingly expensive younger workers.

Swathes of first-rung jobs have disappeared. The result? Many young people are getting caught in the welfare trap, with around one million of them now not in work, education or training.

The question is whether, now the damage has been done, anyone will do what is required to rectify it. Reports suggest that John Healey might go part of the way towards addressing the issue, abandoning Labour's prior pledge to entirely close the gap between the youth and adult rates of the minimum wage. That is good as far as it goes, but it seems unlikely that the Chancellor will take more radical action, such as freezing the rate in cash terms.

The minimum wage, like the triple lock, was introduced with good intentions. But it was never envisaged that it would rise to its current levels. The youth rate has almost doubled in real terms since 1999. It is time for a re-think.

articles.title: McCain predicts Elizabeth Holmes will get a Trump pardon
articles.summary: Meghan McCain, former Sen. John McCain’s (R-Ariz.) daughter, predicts that convicted Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes will get a pardon from President Trump. “One of my hottest, hot takes is that Elizabeth Holmes will eventually get a Trump pardon,” McCain wrote on the social platform X. She shared her thoughts in another post, asking comedian and…
articles.body:
Meghan McCain, former Sen. John McCain’s (R-Ariz.) daughter, predicts that convicted Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes will get a pardon from President Trump.

“One of my hottest, hot takes is that Elizabeth Holmes will eventually get a Trump pardon,” McCain wrote on the social platform X .

She shared her thoughts in another post , asking comedian and satirist Nathan Fielder if he was “aware he just made Elizabeth getting a Trump pardon a lot more likely?”

McCain is referring to Fielder’s “ You Can See Everything ” documentary that followed Holmes in the days before she reported to federal prison.

Holmes was convicted in 2022 of defrauding investors over lofty claims about Theranos’s blood-testing technology, asserting that it could perform several diagnostic tests with only one drop of blood. She is serving her 10-year sentence in Texas but is scheduled to move to a halfway house in Austin, Texas, in August 2027.

Her company attracted several major figures, including media mogul Rupert Murdoch and former Education Secretary Betsy DeVos, to invest in Theranos. Former Secretaries of State Henry Kissinger and George Shultz also sat on the company’s board.

The Theranos founder reportedly asked the Trump administration earlier this year to commute her prison sentence in 2025, according to the Justice Department’s Office of the Pardon Attorney. The office still lists the case as pending, meaning the clemency case “has been opened and the petition is under review.”

Until the status is altered, details about the petition or case cannot be shared, per the Justice Department’s Office of the Pardon Attorney.

During his stints in the White House, Trump has used his pardon power for Jan. 6 rioters and, recently, for two diesel mechanics who were previously charged with and pled guilty to violating the Clean Air Act.

A CBS News analysis from Tuesday reported that Trump’s pardons in his second term have forgiven approximately $1.1 billion in restitution owed to crime victims

This is notably higher than Biden, who forgave $680,000 in his presidential term, according to a study done by the Cato Institute .

articles.title: Discord is making its public communities more searchable, and people have concerns | TechCrunch
articles.summary: In December, messages from Discord's public discoverable servers will begin appearing in search engine results.
articles.body:
Discord announced on Tuesday it will make some conversations in its public servers searchable and easier to find on the internet. The new update targets conversations in “Discoverable Servers,” public Discord servers that administrators have made eligible to appear in the platform’s Server Discovery feature.

The aim is to help people find useful information that might otherwise remain buried in Discord conversations to a wider audience.

According to Discord, more than 63,000 Discoverable Servers host discussions on everything from gaming strategies and fandoms to language learning and niche interests. By making some of these conversations searchable, Discord hopes to extend the reach of its communities beyond the platform itself.

The move also taps into the appeal of traditional internet forums, where users can find answers by searching through publicly accessible discussions. Gaming communities could draw attention to walkthroughs, developers could reach more people with technical advice, and content creators could attract new audiences without relying solely on Discord’s internal discovery tools.

Starting November 16, every Discoverable Server will have its own web page, which may feature automated summaries of discussions in active public channels. Beginning in mid-December, selected messages from public channels may also appear in search engine results.

Server administrators will be able to choose which channels are included, while individual members can opt out of having their messages made publicly searchable. Published messages will not display usernames or avatars. Private servers, direct messages, and group direct messages are excluded.

The announcement has sparked backlash over privacy. Some users are concerned about exposing conversations to audiences far beyond their original context, arguing that posting in a public Discord server does not necessarily mean users want their messages to be discoverable across the wider internet.

Others have raised concerns about whether these conversations could be used to train AI models. Similar arguments emerged during controversies surrounding Reddit’s data-sharing practices and AI training, when users questioned whether their posts and comments should be used to train AI without their explicit consent or compensation.

Discord says users can manage their preferences in settings, while server administrators retain control over which channels participate. Notably, the option to make messages discoverable is turned off by default in the EU, U.K., Canada, Brazil, Australia, and South Korea because of legal restrictions. Teen users are also excluded from the feature.

articles.title: Democrats prep for election interference as Trump administration makes moves
articles.summary: Democrats are preparing for potential election interference after a series of remarks from President Trump and actions from his administration targeting a swath of states. The Justice Department (DOJ) preemptively filed a lawsuit last week in Alaska that could block certification of results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses reelection, arguing that a win for…
articles.body:
Democrats are preparing for potential election interference after a series of remarks from President Trump and actions from his administration targeting a swath of states.

The Justice Department (DOJ) preemptively filed a lawsuit last week in Alaska that could block certification of results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses reelection, arguing that a win for former Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska) could be the result of voter confusion with third candidate Dan J. Sullivan on the ballot.

Trump also appears to have his sights set on Minnesota, writing in a TruthSocial post on Monday that his administration “watching closely” for voter fraud in the state’s Senate race between Republican Michele Tafoya and Democrat Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan.

The Trump administration has taken aim at other states, as well, in the final week leading up to Election Day.

On Monday, a federal appeals court blocked the Justice Department from making California election officials set aside 20,000 ballots in the state that it claimed were from non-citizen voters.

And in Washington State, the DOJ has asked its secretary of state to review a list of over 400 registered voters it believes could also be noncitizens.

When asked on Tuesday if he would respect the midterm results, Trump said he would “if they’re honest elections.”

The efforts have stoked fears among Democrats that the administration could move to challenge election results if the GOP sees widespread victories following Election Day.

“They’re just throwing all of this stuff out there in an attempt to discourage people from believing in the system and trying to discourage people from coming out and registering them to vote, and then actually voting themselves,” former Attorney General Eric Holder said in an interview with CNN on Tuesday.

“Any of these things that they are doing could have been easily done after the election, consistent with the way in which the Justice Department normally operates,” he continued.

Sen. Tina Smith (D-Minn.) accused Trump on Monday of “blatantly laying the groundwork to steal an election.”

“Minnesota will not take kindly to thinly veiled threats from a guy we’ve rejected three times (soon to be four),” Smith wrote in a post on X .

The Democratic National Committee said in a statement Tuesday that it was prepared to counter the administration’s efforts.

“We have grown our voter protection program, with staff based in more than 35 states to train and support election observers all across the country. The DNC’s first-ever in-house litigation team is working tirelessly to defeat attacks on our voting rights as Republicans attempt to make it harder for voters to cast their ballots and hold them accountable for their cost-raising, billionaires-first agenda,” said DNC spokesman Angelo Fernández Hernández.

Rachel Jacobs, a senior partner at the Democratic-aligned Elias Law Group, told The Hill the firm was ready to respond to any actions taken by the administration after the election.

“If and when the election deniers in the Trump administration try similar or new tactics this fall, we will be ready to fight back and ensure that the results are certified according to the will of the voters,” Jacobs said, referring to efforts to overturn the results of the 2020 presidential election.

Minnesota is one of the few states on the Senate map where Republicans could potentially see a pickup opportunity. Last week, the nonpartisan Cook Political Report moved the race toward Republicans from “likely Democrat” to “lean Democrat. Recent polls out of the race show Flanagan narrowly leading Tafoya.

Meanwhile, Alaska’s Senate race is considered much more of a toss-up. The incumbent Sullivan is defending his seat against Peltola, who along with Dan J. Sullivan advanced to the general election as a result of the state’s ranked choice voting system.

The administration has also sought to take action in the deep blue states of California and Washington, citing votes from noncitizens.

On Tuesday, as California voters were in the midst of returning their mail-in ballots, U.S. District Judge David Carter was preparing to hear the case after it was blocked by a federal appeals court .

White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis vowed in a statement that anyone who illegally voted “will be held accountable,” while a Justice Department spokesperson said it makes “no apology for protecting those votes.”

“When this department acts to keep noncitizens from voting, it’s called election interference. That’s a double standard. Enforcing election law right before an election is exactly when it matters most and voters deserve to know their elections are being protected,” the Justice Department spokesperson said.

articles.title: Trump officials say men face a testosterone crisis. Experts say numbers tell different story
articles.summary: American men are facing a crisis in plummeting testosterone levels — at least according to several top Trump administration officials. But experts say there is key context that is being left out of the conversation, and the push towards hormone replacement therapy probably isn’t the panacea that officials believe it to be. Members of President…
articles.body:
American men are facing a crisis in plummeting testosterone levels — at least according to several top Trump administration officials. But experts say there is key context that is being left out of the conversation, and the push towards hormone replacement therapy probably isn’t the panacea that officials believe it to be.

Members of President Trump’s cabinet, like Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., have raised the issue of low testosterone among men repeatedly since they’ve assumed office.

One of Kennedy’s oft-repeated claims is that “an American teenager has less testosterone than a 68-year-old man,” and Hegseth this year rolled out mandatory testosterone testing for active service members over the age of 30.

Personnel found to have low testosterone levels have the option of starting voluntary hormone replacement therapy.

The focus isn’t without cause. Studies conducted in recent decades across the world in countries like the U.S., Denmark and more recently Israel have observed declining testosterone levels among men broadly.

A study published in October , funded by the U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command, found that 25.7 percent of active-duty male Army personnel had a morning testosterone measurement below a threshold of 300 ng/dL, a cutoff used by the American Urological Association (AUA) to support a possible diagnosis of testosterone deficiency in men who are also displaying associated symptoms.

This is not an immediate indication of low testosterone, however, as the hormone can fluctuate widely throughout the day depending on someone’s health and fitness.

According to Claire E. Berryman, a former Pennington Biomedical researcher now at Purdue University and a corresponding author of the study, the findings are not sufficient for diagnosing hypogonadism, a condition where someone has little to no production of sex hormones, on their own.

“A diagnosis generally requires both consistent signs or symptoms of testosterone deficiency and unequivocally and repeatedly low testosterone concentrations. Clinical guidelines recommend confirming low testosterone concentrations with a second morning measurement,” Berryman said.

“Our study provides valuable information about the prevalence of testosterone concentrations below established thresholds, but we did not perform the comprehensive clinical evaluations required to diagnose hypogonadism,” she added.

Researchers in the Army-sponsored study used two thresholds, with one being the AUA’s 300 ng/dL cutoff. They additionally used a 264 ng/dL threshold, which Berryman said came from prior research that established a “harmonized reference range for testosterone concentrations in healthy, nonobese young men.”

The results of the research aligned with what prior studies had found within the general population. Berryman cited a 2018 study that found 30.8 percent of men fell below the 300 ng/dL threshold, though this study encompassed a much wider age range of men aged from 20 to over 60.

Some people, like Kennedy and conservative radio host Alex Jones, have taken this data as evidence that something in the environment is artificially, catastrophically decimating male testosterone levels.

The secretary has previously suggested that chemicals in drinking water are not only wreaking havoc on men’s testosterone levels, but that chemicals could be causing children to become transgender . He and his allies have said Kennedy is simply asking questions, but experts have repeatedly pushed back, saying there is no evidence to support this theory.

Kennedy, 72, has spoken about his own use of “testosterone replacements which are appropriate for my age.”

According to Sandeep Dhindsa, professor of medicine and the chief of the Division of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism at the Saint Louis University School of Medicine, much of the declining testosterone levels observed in recent studies can be attributed to a changing population.

“I think most of the decline in testosterone that would be noticed in studies is going to be the fact that we have an aging population. We have obesity. And when you take into account those factors, then the differences become smaller, but they don’t go away completely,” said Dhindsa.

Whether potential endocrine disruptors like microplastics, chemicals in the environment and phytoestrogens found in plants are to blame is still ” a bit unknown,” according to Dhindsa, who also noted that testosterone levels are highly sensitive to stress and illness.

“In fact, you would be surprised to know that soldiers, for example, if they are going to a war, they have very, very low testosterone levels,” Dhinsa said. “And that’s simply because they’re not getting anything to eat, they’re under high stress, they’re hardly sleeping. So, that’s the body’s normal response.”

Testosterone deficiency is often diagnosed by symptoms like low sex drive, fatigue, depression and erectile dysfunction. In the study sponsored by the Army, Berryman noted that participants were not selected based on symptoms or suspected testosterone deficiency.

Testosterone replacement therapy is prescribed to alleviate these symptoms, not to bring the body’s levels up to a specific number, though Hegseth has said the Pentagon’s screening program was meant to ensure personnel have the “right testosterone levels to operate at your absolute best.”

As the Endocrine Society notes in its brief on testosterone therapy, hormone levels naturally decline with age past the age of 30 and can also temporarily fluctuate due to recent changes like exercising too much, poor nutrition or a severe illness. And the organization states that levels should be tested more than once.

Dhindsa warned that patients often have “unrealistic expectations” of what hormone therapy can do. He noted as an example that after some months of therapy, men might see an increase in muscle mass of 3 to 5 percent, which would not be enough for someone to notice.

“People feel that taking testosterone is almost a solution to many of their ills,” he said. “I can tell you by clinical practice, half of the men I give testosterone to come back in few months, and they say we can’t tell a difference. And the other half usually feel better in terms of their sexual symptom.”

articles.title: 4 Dem senators say Trump should restore canceled green funds to earn trust for permitting reform bill
articles.summary: A group of Democratic senators is expressing distrust that the Trump administration will treat renewable energy fairly under a bipartisan permitting reform bill — and they are calling on the administration to restore climate funding it terminated for blue states. Their letter to Democrats and Republicans who negotiated the bill represents a fracture in the…
articles.body:
A group of Democratic senators is expressing distrust that the Trump administration will treat renewable energy fairly under a bipartisan permitting reform bill — and they are calling on the administration to restore climate funding it terminated for blue states.

Their letter to Democrats and Republicans who negotiated the bill represents a fracture in the Democratic caucus. It’s not entirely clear how widespread the sentiment is among Democrats, but if enough of them vote against the bill, it could hamper its chances.

Sens. Tammy Duckworth (Ill.), Ron Wyden (Ore.), Jeff Merkley (Ore.) and Ed Markey (Mass.) wrote to several Democratic and Republican negotiators that “in seeking our support for BAAJA [the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act], you are asking every Senator to rely on informal assurances from a Trump administration that has proven to be an untrustworthy and erratic negotiating partner and demonstrated a willingness to ignore and violate the plain language of the law.”

“Beyond consideration of the actual text, the promise of BAAJA will only succeed if President Trump takes care that it is faithfully executed. The Trump administration’s record gives us no basis to assume that he will,” they added.

In their letter, the Democrats requested that, as a show of good faith, the Trump administration reinstate billions of dollars in funding it canceled for climate friendly projects in blue states.

“It would be compelling if, before the motion to proceed vote, the Trump administration directed DOE to 1) reinstate every award it terminated in October 2025 that it has not already restored, 2) to allow recipients to draw down those funds under the original award terms and 3) to commit in writing that it will not terminate an award because of the political identity of the recipient’s State or the party affiliation of its elected officials,” they wrote, referring to the Department of Energy.

“While such action may not fully address the wide range of concerns individual Senators have about various portions of this complex legislation, it would represent an important first step and carry far more weight with us and, more importantly, our constituents whose awards were illegally terminated, than mere informal assurances that the Trump administration will stop interfering with clean energy projects,” they added.

The Senate is set to consider the legislation, which would be expected to speed up the buildout for fossil fuel, renewable energy and other projects, including by curtailing certain environmental laws , upon return from its current recess. In fact, it’s expected to take a procedural vote on the floor on whether to advance the legislation fairly immediately upon its return in the lame duck session.

Previous efforts to pass similar legislation were ultimately unsuccessful, but the legislation appears to have at least some bipartisan support heading into its formal consideration.

articles.title: Bank of America kindly asks that you don't share your banking password with your AI assistant | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The banking giant reminds customers that "you're responsible for activity" resulting from your AI agents' access.
articles.body:
Financial giant Bank of America is reminding customers to bank safely by kindly not sharing your banking credentials with your AI agent.

In an email blast to customers titled “Protecting your finances in the Al World,” Bank of America urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, “including an Al-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf.”

You can practically sense the frustration in the person sending the email. Still, customers are increasingly handing over their log-ins as personal AI assistants grow more popular . Sharing your banking username and password with an AI assistant runs the risk that it could do something with your finances without your knowledge, or that your bank thinks someone’s raiding your account and locks you out of it. Worse, a security flaw in the AI assistant could result in it leaking your banking credentials elsewhere, giving financially motivated hackers a way into your bank account.

This latest warning comes as banks are still exploring how AI agents fit into the financial world but are reportedly grappling with unauthorized agents accessing their customers’ money . As we discussed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt , banks, payment providers, and processors are still trying to figure out how to allow customers access to their bank accounts using AI tools, such as for agentic payments, which allow people to set agents to autonomously buy things at the best price or the right time.

A spokesperson for Bank of America confirmed the authenticity of the bank’s email that was posted to social media . But heed the bank’s warning, for if things go wrong, it’s on you. Account agreements at most banks hold customers responsible for anyone they give their log-in to. “If you do share your credentials,” its email reads, “keep in mind that you’re responsible for activity resulting from that access.”

articles.title: Iran war cost increases to $47 billion
articles.summary: The cost of the U.S.’s war against Iran has gone up to $47 billion, an increase of more than $3 billion since last month, as President Trump mulls launching strikes against the Islamic Republic after the U.S. midterm elections. The biggest chunk of the cost is munition replacement at $29 billion, according to an Oct.…
articles.body:
The cost of the U.S.’s war against Iran has gone up to $47 billion, an increase of more than $3 billion since last month , as President Trump mulls launching strikes against the Islamic Republic after the U.S. midterm elections.

The biggest chunk of the cost is munition replacement at $29 billion, according to an Oct. 16 U.S. Central Command (Centcom) estimate, which was shared with Congress and obtained by The Hill on Tuesday.

Nearly $12 billion is obligated for incremental costs of military action and another $6.1 billion to replace equipment losses, according to the estimate. Air Force’s support for deployed personnel, airlift, base, communication support and transportation in theater costs $7.6 billion.

The estimate does not include the cost to damaged U.S. military bases in the Middle East.

The new figure is an update from early September, when the Pentagon said the cost of the conflict, which has gone down in popularity since breaking out in February, was about $43.6 billion.

The estimate also comes as Centcom has drawn up plans to conduct follow-up strikes against Iran if there’s authorization from the White House, The Hill previously reported . The U.S. has a number of strike options in place.

Trump said on Tuesday during his rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, that the U.S. is “making an absolute fortune because of the situation” in the Middle East and predicted that the Iran war would “end very soon.”

The conflict has cost the average American household $2,000 so far, according to Moody’s Analytics.

articles.title: Guardrails Alliance hits Husted over ties to Marc Andreessen in new ad
articles.summary: Super PAC Guardrails Alliance will launch a digital ad campaign Wednesday seeking to tie Ohio Sen. Jon Husted (R)’s past support for data centers to campaign donations he received from tech executives like venture capitalist Marc Andreessen. The 30-second ad, first shared with The Hill, highlights Andreessen’s past donations to Husted’s Senate run against former…
articles.body:
Super PAC Guardrails Alliance will launch a digital ad campaign Wednesday seeking to tie Ohio Sen. Jon Husted (R)’s past support for data centers to campaign donations he received from tech executives like venture capitalist Marc Andreessen.

The 30-second ad, first shared with The Hill, highlights Andreessen’s past donations to Husted’s Senate run against former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio), in which data centers became a major issue for the race over the summer.

“Mark Andreessen has a lot of investments in AI, they’re making him a lot of money,” the ad’s narrator says. “He’s also invested in John Husted’s Senate campaign. What’s he getting from this investment? Well, Jon Husted is a big supporter of data centers … data centers to build AI that makes donors like Mark Andreesen even richer.”

“Even though the experts say AI could kill us all, Husted’s donors get rich and we pay the price,” the narrator continues, referring to AI researchers’ ominous warnings that the technology has the potential to destroy humanity.

Filings from the Federal Election Commission show Andreesen, in his personal capacity, donated $3,500 to Husted’s campaign last November.

Guardrails Alliance was launched last June to counter the AI industry’s spending, including that of Big Tech-aligned super PAC, Leading the Future.

Leading the Future (LTF), launched last year , has received funding from Andreesen’s venture capital firm, Andreessen Horowitz, AI firm Perplexity and tech industry executives like venture capitalist Joe Lonsdale and OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman.

LTF maintains it typically supports candidates who will help advance a “positive, forward-looking agenda for AI innovation” in Washington.

The $100,000 ad buy will run on digital platforms, including premium services offered by platforms like YouTube, across the state of Ohio, according to Guardrails Alliance.

“We’re trying to raise awareness of all the different AI billionaires who are trying to not just oppose regulation, but control every aspect of our lives,” Guardrails Alliance Political Director Charlie Blaettler told The Hill.

“AI billionaires are going to continue to spend money on elections to get their way and to try to buy a Congress that will let industry … write the rules of the road and regulate themselves instead of putting in the commonsense regulations that the vast majority of Americans support,” Blaettler said.

LTF has rejected claims it opposes all AI regulation. A spokesperson for the super PAC previously told The Hill the group “has laid out a clear, positive, and proactive agenda that focuses on establishing a responsible national framework on AI.”

“We’re proud of our track record supporting a diverse array of policymakers and candidates across the country,” the spokesperson added.

Husted is running for a full term after being appointed in 2024 to serve out the remainder of now-Vice President Vance’s Senate term. Brown, a longtime senator who lost his own seat the same year, is looking to take it back this November.

Brown’s campaign has repeatedly hit Husted with messaging targeting his record on data centers. Multiple ads for Brown highlighted Husted’s support of data center developer tax breaks while he was lieutenant governor from 2019 to 2025.

Husted’s campaign has previously emphasized his support for initiatives to make data centers pay for their share of the utility costs.

Senate Democrats blocked Husted’s bill , the Ratepayer Protection Act, in a vote late last month, calling it ineffective and “toothless.”

The bill, which passed the House with bipartisan support, would have required states and some electric utilities to consider a standard under which data centers would have to pay for additional costs caused by their power demand.

The Hill has reached out to Husted’s campaign, Leading the Future and Andreesen Horowitz for comment.

articles.title: Trump announces proposal to loosen methane rules for oil and gas production
articles.summary: President Trump announced plans to loosen methane regulations from the oil and gas sector during a Lubbock, Texas rally Tuesday night. The announcement came during the president’s second campaign stop of the day in Texas, during which he aimed to assist the Senate campaign of Republican Ken Paxton, the state attorney general, in the oil-heavy…
articles.body:
President Trump announced plans to loosen methane regulations from the oil and gas sector during a Lubbock, Texas rally Tuesday night.

The announcement came during the president’s second campaign stop of the day in Texas, during which he aimed to assist the Senate campaign of Republican Ken Paxton, the state attorney general, in the oil-heavy state. Trump told a crowd of supporters he was “officially terminating Biden’s expensive and unnecessary methane regulations.”

The president added the roll back has been in the works for a “long time” with Environmental Protection Agency Administrator (EPA) Lee Zeldin.

The proposed changes are expected to significantly loosen rules governing how the oil and gas industry treats methane, a planet-warming gas that is about 28 times as potent as carbon dioxide.

Among the changes that the administration is expected to propose are looser rules for marginal oil and gas wells, those that produce a relatively small amount of oil but are still estimated to represent about half of the sector’s methane emissions.

In addition, the administration is easing Biden-era restrictions on the industry’s burning of excess gas during oil production, a process known as flaring.

And it is eliminating the Biden administration’s Super Emitter Program requiring energy companies to respond to credible reports of major methane leaks.

A press release from the EPA outlined some additional changes including “flexibility” for deviations in monitoring data, emission control alerts and some emissions test conditions.

The agency also indicated that it would change current standards that require industry vent systems to operate with “no identifiable emissions.”

Overall, the moves are expected to exacerbate climate change but save the industry money; the administration has said that it could save the oil and gas sector $45 billion.

An official has also said the move would enable an additional 210 million barrels of oil production and 1.41 trillion cubic feet of natural gas from 2027 to 2050. The U.S. consumes about 21 million barrels of oil and 92 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day, so this would mean the equivalent of about 10 days’ worth of oil and 15 days’ worth of gas.

When it tightened the regulations on methane in 2023, the Biden administration said that doing so would prevent 58 million tons of methane from entering the atmosphere between 2024 and 2038 — the climate equivalent of taking 28 million gas-powered cars off the road for a year.

articles.title: Amazon updates AI usage rules for engineers, sends memo: We are seeing the beginning of AI’s effect on software engineering
articles.summary: Amazon engineering leaders have updated the role guidelines for Software Development Engineers (SDEs) to reflect that real-world results matter a lot more
articles.body: Amazon engineering leaders have updated the role guidelines for Software Development Engineers (SDEs) to reflect that real-world results matter a lot more than specific tools. A company memo by Terk Terkowitz, vice president and distinguished engineer at Worldwide Amazon Stores, outlined leadership’s vision to move towards “Renaissance Developers” that combine human judgement and artificial intelligence, or AI. They urged engineers to integrate AI into their daily routines or risk being left behind, noting that AI will sit at the center of future engineering practices.Amazon cautioned against evaluating performance solely on “flawed” input metrics, such as the amount of tokens or lines of code, which could increase costs and complexity. Rather, leaders should look to the longer-term impacts on customers and businesses. Engineers were reminded that learning where AI falls short is “a finding, not a failing.” The memo also urged managers and individual contributors to keep their hands on AI tools but stay deeply connected to customer needs, ensuring tech adoption translates into tangible business results.Read full memo Amazon sent to engineersAn update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AIAmazon engineering leaders revised the role guideline for software development engineers, underscoring what matters most is the outcome, not which tools are used.Written by Terk Terkowitz, VP/Distinguished Engineer, Worldwide Amazon StoresOne of the biggest shifts our leadership teams are seeing right now is how AI is changing the way software development engineers (SDEs) do their work, while balancing that the important elements of being an SDE are the same.Engineering leadership, including Distinguished and Senior Principal Engineers, from across Amazon recently came together to reaffirm what it means to be an SDE at Amazon. Based on key learnings and observations from the most successful SDEs at the company, they developed an updated role guideline. Our most prolific engineers have demonstrated that neither the developer role nor their output is defined by the use of AI. We're now in the era of the Renaissance Developer, blending AI tools with human judgment and domain expertise to build entirely new things. As a leader in agentic AI with thousands of SDEs, Amazon believes sharing our vision for the SDE role of the future can serve as a model for our customers.The following is a memo shared with software engineers across Amazon.-TerkDear SDEs and SDMs,As we developed the new version of the role guideline for Software Development Engineers (SDEs) at Amazon, we faced an important question: how much do we focus on AI? Historically we have tried to avoid having the SDE role guidelines be explicit about technology, reflecting the diversity of businesses that Amazon is in, and the work that our SDEs do. We have held to that approach as two decades of technology trends (the cloud, microservices, serverless, etc.) have reshaped the work that SDEs do. In the Senior Principal and Distinguished Engineer communities, we have deeply debated whether this time is different. AI is changing the work of software engineering both more quickly and more fundamentally than these previous trends. What it means to be a software engineer, and what software engineering even is, is changing quickly and durably.Despite the speed of change, we believe that it is still early. We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind. We’re just seeing the beginning of AI’s effect on software engineering. While we have a vision for what the future looks like, there’s a lot that’s still emerging. We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice. If you haven’t already, you should take the time to learn and apply AI into your daily work as soon as possible. If you’re already using AI, keep investing in finding better practice, and keep learning. The pace of change is high.It is difficult to define, in a way that will stand the test of time, what good AI powered engineering practices look like. Any definition we write now will likely look antiquated by this time next year. Antiquated definitions run the risk of slowing our progress, freezing our engineering practices in amber while the world moves on without us. To solve this problem, we have decided to focus on what is not changing as we evolved the SDE roles. Specifically, impact on our customers, our businesses, and our teams. The outcomes that matter aren’t changing, even if the inputs, tools, and techniques are changing faster than ever.“What’s going to change in the next five to ten years?” But I very rarely get asked “What’s not going to change in the next five to ten years?” That second question is actually the more important of the two.Jeff Bezos2012 interview with Werner VogelsThis conclusion made it easier to write the role guideline, but likely leaves you, our SDEs and SDMs, with an important question about how you should be using AI, and how you should be measuring AI usage in your teams and organizations. We believe that it is best to measure, and be measured by, long-term outcomes. But these outcomes can be time delayed, difficult to measure, and hard to isolate from other trends. In some cases, we have tackled those problems by using input metrics instead, like token usage or adoption of AI tools, or throughput metrics like code changes and reviews. We are all aware of how deeply flawed these metrics are, primarily because they are disconnected from what matters. We know that using these metrics could, if used as a target instead of a measure, drive negative outcomes, increasing costs (tokenmaxxing is at odds with frugality), and increasing complexity (measuring LOC is at odds with invent and simplify). We believe that this community, with your strong ownership and focus on delivering results, will help us avoid these negative outcomes.More positively, we have found that these input metrics correlate well with the outputs that matter and expect they will continue to do so for some time. This effect is driven both by increasing productivity and delivery on teams that have embraced AI the most (we call them frontier teams), and that teams and individuals who are not adopting AI or increasing output metrics are falling behind. Using these input metrics, with care and judgement, as you think about your career and your organization’s performance is appropriate. We recommend paying special attention to the 10th percentile (finding those teams who aren’t embracing AI effectively and understanding why) and the 90th percentile (finding those teams who are heavily using AI and understanding whether they’re seeing delivery increases to match) of AI adoption. Working together, over time, we will find better metrics and set smarter goals.“Good inventors and designers deeply understand their customer. They spend tremendous energy developing that intuition. They study and understand many anecdotes rather than only the averages you’ll find on surveys.”Jeff Bezos2016 Letter to ShareholdersTo paraphrase: Good leaders deeply understand their team's work. They spend tremendous energy developing that intuition. They study and understand many anecdotes, and carefully track outputs, rather than only surface-level metrics.If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing. Document why, share it with your community of peers, bring it to your manager, and work to find solutions. An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for.As a technical or organizational leader, part of your job is making sure that your team or organization is using AI to the best effect to improve delivery for customers and your business. That requires deeply understanding these technologies yourself, working with them hands-on rather than relying on what you hear, and understanding how others are using them. Sufficient understanding means you have used these tools on your production work, can describe a task where they helped and a task where they did not, and can explain that judgement to your team. Deploying AI in your organizations requires carefully balancing between exploring new and better ways to do things and investing in doubling down on the ones you already have. Judgement and care are key. As a leader, we expect you to be taking ownership of connecting the inputs and outputs in your team or organization.As we have looked across our organizations, we have found that the leaders who are having the most impact are those doubling down on learn and be curious. Both spending the time they need to learn AI and making time for the people they lead to do the same. We have seen that the returns on this investment in our organizations are disproportionately large, with teams who have followed their curiosity (appropriately balanced with deliver results and insist on the highest standards) seeing the most positive impact from AI adoption.We have also found that SDEs and SDMs who are closer to their products and businesses are able to take the most advantage of AI and agentic software development. As Amazon has grown, we’ve seen some of our ICs and SDMs become less connected to their customers and business. We want to reverse this trend. We recommend that ICs of all levels find ways to become deeply connected to your customers, and your team or org’s product direction. As always, the scope and depth of this ownership will increase as you become more senior. For SDMs, we also recommend spending time making sure you’re close to your customers and business, and you’re helping the ICs in your organization to do the same.This is a time of change for our industry, and a time of change for what it means to be a software engineer. We believe that the opportunity for software, and for software engineers, has never been larger. We’re more excited about the future of software development, and of our role as engineers, than ever before. Partnering with you as strong, curious, customer-obsessed owners, we will invent the future of software development together.We will continue to evolve the SDE role over the coming years, as AI’s effect on our business and engineering practices becomes clear. But we believe that’s unlikely to change what really matters: obsession with our customers, and a long-term focus on delivering results.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: BlackBerry, the iconic brand whose physical-keyboard devices once dominated the early smartphone era, is putting its money into the growth of artificial
articles.body: BlackBerry, the iconic brand whose physical-keyboard devices once dominated the early smartphone era, is putting its money into the growth of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered robots. Following years of operational restructuring, the Canadian technology company has evolved from a consumer mobile phone giant into an embedded software specialist. Now, as CEO John Giamatteo steers the enterprise past its automotive foundations, autonomous machines and “physical AI” seems to have taken center stage, as per a report by CNBC.Blackberry moving beyond smartphone and carsBlackBerry’s core engine today is its QNX operating system. While best known for powering vehicle components ranging from electronic braking to semi-autonomous driving features, QNX is already running inside more than 275 million vehicles globally. However, executive leadership sees the next commercial frontier outside passenger cars.“While the products we sell today can’t be held in the palm of your hand, they’re pervasive around you. 275 million cars, robots, governments, medical instrumentation, supply chain. That’s the new BlackBerry, and that’s what’s driving all of our growth,” Giamatteo told CNBC.Unlike generative AI models that generate text, video or synthetic images, physical AI equips mechanical systems to perceive, navigate and safely interact with physical environments. Giamatteo noted that robotics has quickly become one of the fastest-growing segments inside the QNX portfolio. The company is leaning on decades of automotive safety certifications to position QNX as the foundational, mission-critical operating software that keeps commercial machines operating reliably.Expanding backlog and financial turnaroundThe pivot toward automated machinery is already feeding the company’s forward financial pipeline. According to the report, BlackBerry recently disclosed that its QNX royalty backlog crossed $1.2 billion, expanding by more than $250 million across two quarters. Giamatteo attributed that momentum to global automakers shifting toward sophisticated centralised computing architectures, an expanded portfolio of enterprise software solutions and accelerating customer demand for physical AI deployments.BlackBerry's stock has surged 142% just in 2026, a remarkable reversal of fortunes for a company that had been written off as dead after the emergence of touch screen rivals, including Apple's iPhone.Deepening integration with NvidiaKey to BlackBerry's robotics expansion is its technical relationship with chipmaker Nvidia. Originally established for automotive projects, the alliance has widened across industrial automation. Giamatteo confirmed that Nvidia has “standardised on QNX as the platform of choice” for its Halos Safety Stack.“That has opened up so many doors, an incredible pipeline of opportunity,” Giamatteo said. According to the CEO, that collaboration is directly driving QNX adoption across autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), robotic forklifts, and automated warehouse sleds ferrying pallet cargo to loading docks.You use AI every day.
